title: Miniworkload smoke harness to surface microburst p95 drift
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Add a lightweight per-PR miniworkload harness that runs in the CI smoke stage to quickly surface regression signals for p95 and tokens/sec during microburst scenarios. The harness runs a compact set of synthetic traffic patterns (short, medium, microburst) using the same request encoder/seed prompts as production; it computes a compact fingerprint (quantized p50/p95, tokens/sec, tail-slope) and emits a delta-score versus the rolling baseline. Goal: catch high-confidence slowdowns introduced by PRs earlier than full-scale bench runs, with <15s walltime per job and stable false-positive rate under 2%.
acceptance_criteria: CI job executes in under 20s on the CI runner (median across runs)
Delta-score computed and attached to PR comment with link to detailed grafana trace when score > threshold
False positive rate empirically < 2% over a 30-run historical testset
Produces compact baseline snapshot and supports rolling baseline window (7 days) for comparison
Does not require additional dedicated GPUs in hosted CI; relies on lightweight quantized model variants
implementation_notes: Create a miniworkload binary that reuses existing bench harness libs but restricts sequence lengths and sample count to bound time
Fingerprint consists of: p50_ms (ms), p95_ms (ms), tokens_per_sec (avg), tail_slope_ratio (p95/p50) — stored as 8-byte floats in artifact
Use a bootstrap/permutation test to compute significance of delta rather than simple percent change to reduce FP rate
Attach a tiny JSON artifact to the CI run with baseline_id, delta_score, and deterministic seed to allow replay
Add a PR action that posts human-readable summary and links to perf-grafana panel and synthetic trace when delta_score exceeds threshold
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Noise from CI runner variability could increase false positives. Mitigation: run 3 quick sub-samples and median-aggregate; require consistent delta across sub-samples
Risk: Developers may get alert fatigue. Mitigation: calibration period with opt-in telemetry and adjustable threshold per repo
Risk: Maintenance overhead for baseline snapshots. Mitigation: auto-prune baseline window and store compact fingerprints only
Trade-off: Not all regressions detectable at miniworkload size; acceptance that this catches high-signal regressions early and defers low-signal to full bench runs
